To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a DPR based HTH is capable of severely compromising the randomness of a TRNG.
we developed and demonstrated an attack on a FPGA based TRNG that exploits the DPR capability of FPGAs.

1) the DPR feature of modern FPGAS is a potential vulnerability that can be exploited to insert a HTH that severely degrades the randomness of a TRNG, 2) the HTH is stealthy and difficult to detect, and 3) the attack is effective even when the TRNG has a high entropy source, and the Trojan is inserted in an FPGA with a high degree of reconfiguration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the security of FPGA based TRNGs against a class of attacks that are not considered in the literature, and is the first to report such a threat.
the security of TRNGs, which are widely used as a source of randomness in cryptographic protocols and algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DPR capability of modern FGPAs can be exploited to launch a novel, in-field attack that can significantly affect the randomness of a practical TRNG.
our attack is the first to demonstrate that a DPR-enabled TRNG can be successfully attacked from a remote device, without any access to the target device.
our attack is very practical and can easily be implemented in the field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a practical FPGA based TRNG, which is a critical component for several security applications, could be severely affected by an adversary who can remotely insert an HTH in the FPGA.
we present a novel attack on a practical TRNG that can be mounted remotely, without physical access to the device.
the attack is a practical and low-cost method of reducing the randomness of a TRNG, and can be easily implemented on the FPGA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DPR feature of modern FPGAS is a doubleedged sword.
the DPR feature of modern FPGAS can be exploited to mount attacks on the TRNG, and that this is a significant security threat that needs to be addressed.
DPR capability of modern FGPAs can be exploited by a remote attacker to compromise a practical TRNG in an in-field manner, without requiring any physical access to the device.
